# CONTRADICTIONS with the three ticket summaries

These are the ones that should change your plan.

### 1. No doc treats the product card as one shared component with those four variants — CRITICAL for SFCC-236

- **Page 1 models it as three separate modules**: `Product Card Base`, `Product Card Group`, `Product Cards with Lookbook`. `Product Card Base`'s Variants/Configurations cell is `—` (empty). The only variant list anywhere is **"3-up, 4-up"**, which is a *grid density* on Product Card Group — an entirely different axis from Homepage/PLP/Wishlist/Recently-Viewed.
- **Page 3 models it as a fourth, differently-named thing**: `Product Tile`, owned by the **PLP** epic, whose variant axes are **"per-colour variant tiles; hover image vs video; large/featured merchandised tile variant"** — again a completely different set from the ticket's four.
- **Page 3 also lists `wishlist item card with availability` as a separate component** under the Wishlist epic (SFCC-8), and **page 2 lists `wishlist product card` as a separate Sep 21 / Sprint 5 design deliverable** — i.e. the Wishlist variant is scheduled as its own design item, not as a variation of an already-locked card.
- **Only page 2 states the one-shared-component principle**, and it names **PDP, PLP and Homepage** — three surfaces. **Wishlist and Recently Viewed Full History are not in that list.**

Net: the ticket's "ONE shared component with Homepage / PLP / Wishlist / Recently Viewed Full History variants driven by a style prop" is a **synthesis that exists in no document**. Four different names are in play across the docs — Product Card Base, Product Card Group, Product Tile, wishlist item card — plus Product Cards with Lookbook.

### 2. The design for three of SFCC-236's four variants is not due to be finalised yet, and per the docs' own freeze rule the story cannot be written

Page 2's rules say stories are written only against locked designs, and that all variations must be locked under the earliest epic (PDP, **Aug 13 / Sprint 3**). But page 2's own tracker schedules:

| Variant | Design finalised | Stories dev-ready |
|---|---|---|
| PDP (product card) | Aug 13 (Sprint 3) ✅ passed | Aug 24 |
| **PLP** (product grid) | **Sep 7 (Sprint 4)** — not yet reached | Sep 21 |
| **Homepage** | **Sep 7 (Sprint 4)** — not yet reached | Sep 21 |
| **Wishlist** (wishlist product card) | **Sep 21 (Sprint 5)** — not yet reached | Oct 5 |

Today is 2026-09-02. **Three of the four named variants are behind future design-lock dates.** Page 2's rule that all variations must be locked under PDP has already been broken by page 2's own schedule. Building SFCC-236 now means either building against unlocked designs or accepting rework — page 2's hard rule says any post-lock change "requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component."

### 3. Recently Viewed surfaces contradict the ticket — PLP is not listed anywhere, mini-bag and account are

Ticket says **PLP / PDP / Cart**. Docs say:

| Source | Surfaces |
|---|---|
| Page 1 (`04.7`) | **PDP** only |
| Page 3, PDP row | "on many pages" (unspecified) |
| Page 3, Recommendation Carousels row | "across **PDP, cart, mini-bag, and account**" |

**PLP appears on no list.** **Mini-bag and account appear on the docs' list but not the ticket's.** The only explicit surface enumeration in any of the three pages is `PDP, cart, mini-bag, and account` — a 4-surface list that overlaps the ticket's on only two. This needs resolving before SFCC-83 is scoped, since mini-bag and account are materially different mount points from PLP.

### 4. Recently Viewed design status is contradictory across pages

Page 1: **✅ Done, confirmed by Dennis 2026-08-10.** Page 3: **PENDING / PENDING sign-off on both of its rows**, with the most recent note (07-07) reading *"Full history still pending"*. Page 1 is the newer assertion but page 3 has 44 versions to page 1's 13 and is the page the client actually reviews in the weekly design meeting. Do not treat "Done" on page 1 as sign-off — page 3 is where Zimmermann sign-off is recorded, and it says Pending.

### 5. SFCC-84 has no design at all, and the fundamental design question is open

There is no See Full History page in any inventory, template list, or epic scope. The only guidance is two open questions from June/July:
- *"2 options: Wishlist/Search Results … Look like the wishlist or like a search page"* — undecided
- *"Conscious choice for minimal info, no price no product name?"* — undecided

That second one matters for SFCC-236 too: if the recently-viewed card genuinely drops price and product name, that is a **content-reduction variant**, not a styling variant, and a single `style` prop over a shared card may not be the right shape.

### 6. Sprint assignment for Recently Viewed is contradictory three ways

Page 3 PDP row says **Sprint 1-2**. Page 3 Recommendation Carousels row says **Sprint 2**. Page 1 says **Sprint 3 (for user story writing, 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-24)**. Page 2 puts the owning epic across **Sprint 2, 3, 4** with dev-ready Sep 7. Four sources, four answers.

### 7. The docs' component taxonomy does not match the codebase's

The repo uses `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/`. The docs use **Component / Sub-component / Module / Template**, with no mapping between the two. Under page 1's taxonomy the product card is a **Module** with two **Sub-components** (Image Carousel, Wishlist Icon) — which maps most naturally to an *organism*, not an atom or molecule. Worth settling the mapping before scaffolding, because "Product Card Base + Image Carousel + Wishlist Icon" is a three-component build under the docs, not one.

---

# Two extra findings worth knowing

**`04.71 Writing User Stories for Components` (page ID 400195600, version 2)** is a sibling of pages 1 and 2 under the same parent and is directly load-bearing for how SFCC-236 should be split. It defines **Level 1 component epics** vs **Level 2 page epics**, and rules that a **PWA Kit only** component (its examples: Button, Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item) gets **one story in the PWA Kit epic only**, while a **Contentful + PWA Kit** component gets two. Page 1 classifies every product-card and Recently Viewed row as **PWA Kit** — so under 04.71 these are single-story components with no Contentful counterpart. It also says Level 2 page stories "should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1."

**`Design Decision Tracker` (page ID 449282049, version 1)** is the third child of `04.7` and is **completely empty** — no content body at all. Given the volume of unresolved decisions surfaced above (full-history layout, minimal-info card, wishlist-vs-search), this looks like a page created for exactly this purpose and never filled in.

All three target pages have **zero comments**.</result>

...
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_GROUP_RECIPE, { isPaginated });   // line 139

It is both the one you named and objectively the most recently added (git-touched `2026-09-01 19:28`, tied with `zimmColourSwatch`, from the in-flight SFCC-91 branch). Path: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`.

**(1) `index.tsx` — the component.** Naming: folder is `camelCase` with a `zimm` prefix; the exported symbol is the `PascalCase` form (`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`).

Export style is **both** — named plus default:

The default export exists specifically so `React.lazy()` can consume it — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:74` does `React.lazy(() => import('../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup'))`. Consumers that don't need lazy use the named form (`zimmProductContent/index.tsx:3-5` imports three atoms by name; `product-detail/index.tsx:64` imports `{ ZimmProductMeta }`). **Not all ui-kits components have a default export** — `zimmProductContent` and `zimmProductMeta` are named-only. Exported alongside it is the *data* type `ZimmColourSwatchValue` (line 20), which the story and test both import (`index.stories.tsx:6`, `index.test.tsx:8`) — matching `.claude/rules/components.md:17-22`'s "shared consumption" trigger. ```tsx

...
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_GROUP_RECIPE, { isPaginated });   // line 139

That second argument is the props object fed to the recipe's `baseStyle` function. ## 7. BLAST RADIUS

### `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`
**Zero importers — the directory does not exist.**

The blast radius is entirely *prospective*, and it is created by the overrides resolver rather than by direct imports. The moment `overrides/app/components/product-tile/index.tsx` exists, every base-path import of `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile` issued **from inside `node_modules`** is silently redirected to your file.

**Base importers of `components/product-tile` — 8 lines across 6 files (3 non-test):**

| File | Line | What |
|---|---|---|
| `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx` | 17 | `import ProductTile` — **redirected** |
| `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/index.jsx` | 53 | `import ProductTile, {Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}` — **redirected** |
| `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx` | 57 | `product-tile/promo-callout` (subpath) |
| `.../components/product-tile/index.jsx` | 32 | self-import of `promo-callout` |
| `.../components/product-tile/index.test.js` | 8 | base test |
| `.../components/product-tile/promo-callout.test.js` | 11, 15 | base tests |
| `.../utils/product-utils.test.js` | 26 | mock fixture |

**So overriding `product-tile` immediately changes PLP, Search, Home (via ProductScroller), Cart, PDP, and empty-search-results — all at once, with no code change in any of those pages.** Two of the redirected call sites depend on the **named `Skeleton` export** (`product-list/index.jsx:52` and its render at `:607`), so **any override must re-export `Skeleton` or PLP breaks at import time.** This is the single highest-risk fact in this report.

**Importers in `overrides/` — 3, and all three are `promo-callout` only, not the tile:**
- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:74`
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx:5`
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.test.tsx:17` (a `vi.mock`)

## Summary of gaps to resolve before you estimate

1. **No recently-viewed data source exists.** Einstein's `viewed-recently-einstein` is the only server-side option and it will not satisfy SFCC-84's "all recently viewed items." A client-side history store is net-new work with no scaffolding (`useLocalStorage` from commerce-sdk-react is `@internal` and read-only).
2. **`CardBaseline` is not a thing.** SFCC-236 cannot "extend" it. Any planning that assumed an existing shared card is starting from zero.
3. **Creating `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` silently rewires six base pages** the instant the file lands, and PLP will fail at import unless the named `Skeleton` export is preserved.

This one is *not* a gap, contrary to how it's framed. The spec exists as a confirmed requirement row: **CRM-132 on 04.1.11 (ID 302022672)** gives the exact field list — image, name, price, sale price or What's Now price where applicable, size, colour. - **The two component trackers disagree and one is stale.** 1.5 Web Design (268075023, page-level, blank last-updated) vs 04.7/04.72 (component-level). content.text:
Verified independently — the sweep was right, and it changes the shape of this build. Confluence is still running; here's what's already settled.

## The thing that matters most

**SFCC-236 has no foundation to build on.** `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` does not exist. Neither does `CardBaseline` — it appears exactly three times in the repo, all of them prose in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (lines 128, 181, 186), describing a file and an export that have never been written. Zero occurrences in any `.ts`/`.tsx`.

Worth naming: the skill told me that where `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` disagrees with `overrideStyling.md`, **the rules file wins**. Here that precedence rule points the wrong way — the handbook correctly lists `product-tile` as still-base, and the rules file is the stale one. I checked the filesystem rather than trusting either.

**And there's a live trap in the obvious approach.** The moment `overrides/app/components/product-tile/index.tsx` exists, the overrides resolver silently redirects every base import to it — PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results all change with no edit to any of them. Worse:

```
import ProductTile, {
    Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile'
```

That's `pages/product-list/index.jsx:51-53`. An override missing a named `Skeleton` export **breaks PLP at import time**. Building the card in `ui-kits/` instead keeps the blast radius to files that explicitly import it.

## Three more that change scope

- **Recently Viewed has no data source.** Zero hits for `recentlyViewed`/`browsingHistory` across overrides, `retail-react-app`, and `commerce-sdk-react`. No SFCC API. The only thing that exists is the Einstein recommender string `viewed-recently-einstein` — which your PDP override already renders at `product-detail/index.tsx:1007`. So SFCC-83 on PDP is a *replacement*, and SFCC-84's "full history" is something Einstein structurally cannot return.
- **Three of SFCC-236's four surfaces have no page override** — PLP, Cart and Wishlist are all base-only. And base Wishlist renders `ProductItem` (a row), not a card at all.
- **Your own PRDs contradict the ACs.** `plp.md §2.5` (SPR-14, Confirmed) and `account.md` CRM-113 both require a **save-to-wishlist icon on every tile**. SFCC-236 is *labelled* SPR-14 — but no AC mentions it. Separately, `search.md §7.4` says Recently Viewed is **PDP and Cart**, and explicitly lists PLP under *"do not implement on those surfaces until confirmed"* — while SFCC-83 names PLP as a confirmed surface.

## Sprint reality

All three are in **SFCC Sprint 4**, which ends **7 Sep** — five days. SFCC-236 is 8 points, SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are 2 each. For calibration, PR #64 (SFCC-89, static product info — no variants, no hover states, no new page) was **43 files**.

## What I need from you

The Figma gate is still the hard blocker. Concretely, to unblock SFCC-236 I need node URLs for:

| Variation | States needed |
|---|---|
| PLP | default · desktop hover · out-of-stock · mobile |
| Homepage | default · desktop hover · mobile |
| Wishlist | default · desktop hover |
| Recently Viewed Full History | default · desktop hover · mobile |
| **Recently Viewed rail** (SFCC-83) | default — **no rail component exists in the DS at all**, only a tile-level `Recently Viewed Product` |
| **See Full History page** (SFCC-84) | page frame — desktop + mobile |

I'll fold in the Confluence findings and put the full gate table in front of you as soon as that sweep returns. Nothing gets planned or built until you've seen it.

---

# TASK A — Wishlist (CRM, page 302022672 v16)

**No wishlist row on this page is struck through.** The page contains exactly 6 strikethrough instances (CRM-004, CRM-008, CRM-065a, CRM-070a, CRM-086a, CRM-096a) — all unrelated to wishlist. Every row below is live and **Status = Confirmed**.

### The one row that actually specifies wishlist tile contents

**CRM-132** | Sub-Area: *Wishlist - My Account* | Owner: Accenture | Storefront: ALL | Custom | **Confirmed** | Comments: *(empty)* | Not struck through
> "The system will display the customer's saved wishlist items on the My Account Wishlist page showing product image, product name, price, sale price or What's Now price where applicable, size and colour for each item"

### Wishlist — PLP entry points

- **CRM-113** (Custom, Confirmed, no comments): "The system will display the Wishlist star icon on each product tile on the PLP"
- **CRM-114** (Custom, Confirmed): "The system will allow logged-in customers to add an in-stock product to their Wishlist from the PLP by clicking the star icon on the product tile"
- **CRM-115** (Custom, Confirmed): "The system will display a size selection popover on the product tile showing available in-stock sizes when the star icon is clicked"
- **CRM-116** (Custom, Confirmed): "The system will save the wishlist item at size level upon the customer selecting a size from the popover"
- **CRM-117** (Custom, Confirmed): "The system will only display in-stock sizes in the PLP size selection popover"
- **CRM-118** (**Config**, Confirmed): "The system will allow the customer to remove a product from their Wishlist from the PLP by clicking the active star icon"
- **CRM-119** (Custom, Confirmed): "The system will prompt guest customers to log in or create an account when attempting to add an item to the Wishlist from the PLP"

### Wishlist — PDP entry points

- **CRM-120**: "The system will allow logged-in customers to add an in-stock product to their Wishlist from the PDP by selecting a size and clicking the star icon"
- **CRM-121**: "The system will require the customer to select a size before an item can be saved to the Wishlist"
- **CRM-122**: "The system will display a prompt if the customer attempts to wishlist a product without first selecting a size"
- **CRM-123**: "The system will only allow in-stock and out-of-stock sizes to be added to the Wishlist" — **Comments: "@Emma Kirwan I have changed this requirement to allow out of stock & in stock sizes to be added to the wishlist - Based on the enhancement"**
- **CRM-124**: "The system will save wishlist items at size level"
- **CRM-125**: "The system will display the star icon in an active state on the PDP when the selected size is already saved to the customer's Wishlist"
- **CRM-126**: "The system will allow the customer to remove a product from their Wishlist from the PDP by clicking the active star icon"
- **CRM-127**: "The system will only allow one size per product to be saved to the Wishlist"
- **CRM-128**: "The system will not allow the customer to add a product to the Wishlist in a different size if that product is already saved"
- **CRM-129**: "The system will prompt guest customers to log in or create an account before adding an item to the Wishlist from the PDP"

All Custom, Confirmed, comments empty except CRM-123.

### Wishlist — Global

- **CRM-130** (Owner: **Dependent SF Functionality**, Confirmed): "The system will maintain a single global wishlist per customer visible across all regional storefronts"
- **CRM-131** (Accenture, Confirmed): "The system will display regional availability for each wishlist item - items unavailable in the customer's current region will remain visible but marked as unavailable"

### Wishlist — My Account (rest of section)

- **CRM-133** (Dependent SF Functionality): "The system will not enforce a maximum limit on the number of items a customer can save to their Wishlist"
- **CRM-134**: "The system will display a wishlist item in a greyed out unavailable state if the product is not available in the customer's current region, without removing it from the wishlist"
- **CRM-135**: "The system will display a notification banner at the top of the Wishlist page when an action is performed (item moved to cart, wishlist shared)"
- **CRM-136**: "The system will allow the customer to add a wishlist item to the shopping bag"
- **CRM-137**: "The system will remove the item from the Wishlist upon successful add to bag"
- **CRM-138**: "The system will allow the customer to remove items from the Wishlist page without adding them to the bag"
- **CRM-139** (Dependent SF Functionality): "The system will persist the Wishlist globally for registered customers across sessions, devices, store view switches and regions"
- **CRM-140**: "The system will support a configurable rule for automatic removal of wishlist items after a defined period of inactivity" — **Comments: "Suggested threshold 18 months - OOTB SFCC for guest users is 7 days for logged in users we need to define custom logic to clear wishlist"**
- **CRM-141**: "The system will allow the customer to share their Wishlist via email by entering one or more recipient email addresses and an optional message"
- **CRM-142**: "The system will send a share notification email to the entered recipients containing links to each product in the customer's Wishlist"
- **CRM-143**: "The system will trigger the share Wishlist email to the customer"

### Peripheral wishlist mentions

- **CRM-017**: "…persistent navigation panel within the My Account area containing the following sections - My Account, Orders, Returns, Wishlist, Account Details, Address Book, Saved Cards, Gift Cards, Communications Preferences and Logout"
- **CRM-025**: "The system will display a **static teaser** and a link to view the customer's full wishlist when a customer lands on the account dashboard. The system will navigate the customer to the Wishlist page when the view link is selected. Wishlist data will be stored and managed within SFCC"
- **CRM-144** (*Back in Stock Notifications*): "The system will send back-in-stock notifications for wishlist items to the customer based on the regional availability of the region in which the item was originally added to the wishlist"
- **CRM-172** (*Global vs Local*): "The system will maintain orders, returns, wishlist, account details, address book and communication preferences as global data accessible across all regional storefronts"

### Direct answers to your Task A questions

- **What's displayed per entry:** image, name, price, sale price *or* **"What's Now price"** where applicable, **size**, **colour** (CRM-132). Remove is specified (CRM-138). Add-to-bag is specified (CRM-136) — but only as an *action*, never as a button on the tile. No wishlist-star, no quick-add, no badge, no hover-image-swap, no colour swatches, no product-count is specified.
- **Product or SKU/size level:** **SKU/size level**, unambiguously — CRM-116, CRM-124. Plus a hard constraint most people miss: **one size per product max** (CRM-127, CRM-128).
- **Grid of tiles?** **NOT SPECIFIED.** No CRM row says grid, tile, card, columns, or responsive layout for the Wishlist page. CRM-132 says "display… items"; CRM-025 calls the dashboard version a "static teaser". Compare SPR-01/SPR-55 which explicitly say "grid layout" for PLP and search. **The wishlist page has no documented layout requirement at all.**

---

# TASK B — Homepage (HPC, page 303071234 v14)

Page read in full: **HPC-001 → HPC-040**, all Confirmed, no strikethrough anywhere on the page.

**The Homepage requirements page specifies NOTHING about product tile / product card / product grid / product carousel contents. Explicitly: there is no such row.** All 40 rows fall into: Content Model & CMS Authoring (001–012), Consent & Cookie (013–014), Navigation — Header (015–029), Navigation — Footer (030–038), Chat Integration (039–040).

Closest adjacent rows, verbatim:

- **HPC-009** | Content Model & CMS Authoring | Confirmed | no comments:
  > "The system should support editorial modules including campaign imagery, collection features and **product spotlights**."
  
  This is the only mention of anything product-shaped on the homepage. It does not define contents, does not say tile/card/grid/carousel, and does not say how products are selected.

- **HPC-001** | Confirmed | **Comments: "Open Discussion: Product Names/Prices - SFCC vs Contentful - Review with @Tim Lavelle @Jasmijn Tsang"**
  > "The system should serve all homepage content from Contentful as the sole CMS across all regional storefronts."
  
  Directly relevant to SFCC-236: whether a homepage product card gets its name/price from SFCC or Contentful is an **open discussion, unresolved**. That's a data-source decision, not just a display one.

- **HPC-010**: "The system should support reusable page builder templates across page types."

Two data-quality observations on this page: row **HPC-008** is written as `/HPC-008` (stray slash), and the **Chat Integration row before HPC-040 has a blank Req ID** (implied HPC-039). Neither affects your analysis but they'll bite anyone grepping by ID.

---

# TASK C — Additional cross-surface price constraints

Excluding PRC-08 / PRC-09 / PRC-33 as instructed, from 04.1.12 (302612483 v11):

**PRC-17** | Sub-Area: VIC & Customer Group Pricing | Accenture | ALL | Custom | **Confirmed** | Comments: *(empty)* | Not struck through
> "The system will support customer-group-specific catalogue pricing in SFCC, such that customers in a configured discount group see their discounted price **consistently across PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended product tiles and wishlist**. Discounts will not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards."

This is a genuinely additional constraint on your shared component: the price slot must be able to render a **third pricing state** — customer-group/VIC price — on Wishlist and recommended-product tiles, distinct from RRP and from was/now sale. And per PRC-18, "Customer group discounts will prevail over sale pricing," so the component needs a precedence rule, not just three variants.

**Homepage appears in zero PRC surface lists** — PRC-08, 09, 17, 33 and 41 all enumerate PLP/PDP/mini-bag/cart/checkout/wishlist/recommended tiles/order history. Homepage is never named. Combined with HPC-001's open discussion, **nothing in the functional requirements guarantees a homepage product card shows a price at all, or where that price comes from.**

---

# CRITICAL — where the surfaces diverge

### 1. Blocking conflict: the PLP tile's icon is contradicted between two Confirmed pages

**SPR-14** (04.1.9, v14) | Confirmed | **Comments: "Changed FR to cart icon - wishlist on product card in PLP is not part of the new designs CC: @Dani Rivett"**
> "The system will display a ~~save-to-wishlist~~ **cart** icon on each product tile on the PLP"

**SPR-15** | Confirmed | **Comments: "Changed FR from wishlist to cart on PLP product tile functionality. CC: @Dani Rivett"**
> "The system must prompt the shopper to select a size when they tap the ~~wishlist~~ **cart** icon on a PLP tile, so that entries are saved at SKU/size level rather than product level"

These directly contradict **CRM-113 / CRM-114 / CRM-115 / CRM-117 / CRM-118**, which are all still live, unstruck, and Confirmed, and still say the **wishlist star icon** sits on the PLP tile with an in-stock-sizes popover. The SPR page was updated to reflect new designs; the CRM page was not. Both are "source of truth" pages at the same extraction date.

This is the single most important thing to resolve before SFCC-236 is estimated — it decides whether the shared card's action slot is one icon or two, and whether the PLP variant needs the wishlist affordance at all. Route it to Dani Rivett / Jasmijn Tsang.

### 2. Wishlist tile requires two fields no other tile spec includes

CRM-132 mandates **size** and **colour** per entry. The PLP tile spec (**SPR-10**: "product image, name, and price") and the search tile spec (**SPR-56**: "product image, product name, and price") mandate neither. Note SPR-11 — "The system will show each possible colour variant for a product as a separate tile" — means PLP encodes colour *by tile identity*, not as a printed label. Wishlist cannot do that, because it's saved at a specific SKU. **Structurally different content model, not just a different style prop.**

Also unique to Wishlist: **"What's Now price"** (CRM-132) — a named price type that appears nowhere in the PRC page or in SPR-12's Was/Now wording. Worth confirming whether it's a distinct concept or a typo for "Was/Now".

### 3. Wishlist tile needs two states no other tile has

**CRM-131** and **CRM-134** require a **greyed-out "unavailable in your region"** state that keeps the item visible. Nothing equivalent exists for PLP — **SPR-31** does the opposite, *demoting or suppressing* out-of-stock products from category and search results. Same component, inverted availability behaviour.

### 4. PLP tile requires three behaviours the Wishlist tile has no basis for

- **SPR-13**: hover swap between model and flat/item image on desktop
- **SPR-16**: product badges (RUNWAY, CAMPAIGN, etc.), multiple per product
- **SPR-17**: Quick Add to Bag with size prompt, without navigating to PDP

None appear in any wishlist requirement. Conversely CRM-136/137 require an add-to-bag that **removes the item from the wishlist on success** — a side effect a PLP quick-add must not have.

### 5. Surfaces with NO documented tile spec at all

- **Homepage** — no tile contents, no selection logic, no layout, no price guarantee. Only HPC-009's "product spotlights" and an unresolved SFCC-vs-Contentful data-source question (HPC-001).
- **Wishlist page layout** — contents specified (CRM-132), but grid/tile/card/responsive layout is never stated anywhere. 04.1.18 (303333385 v3) only says "The system will deliver page templates for login, registration, password reset, order history, order details, returns history, address book, saved payments and **wishlist**" — a template will exist; its shape is undefined.
- **Recently Viewed Full History page** — **does not exist as a requirement.** The only trace is **PRD-027** (04.1.8, v18), Confirmed: *"The system should display a 'Recently Viewed' carousel based on the customer's browsing session history"*, with **Comments: "Updated design: not a carousel but with button 'See full history'"**. That comment is the sole documentary basis for the whole page. **SPR-61** scopes Recently Viewed to "the PDP and Cart page" only. No requirement defines the full-history page's existence, route, tile contents, layout, or pagination. Treat it as undocumented scope.

### Net read for SFCC-236

One component can plausibly serve **PLP + Search + Homepage**, since Homepage is undefined and Search matches PLP almost exactly (SPR-10 ≈ SPR-56). **Wishlist is the outlier** — it needs printed size + colour, a "What's Now" price type, a region-unavailable greyed state, a VIC price state, and destructive add-to-bag. That's five variations, three of which change the *data contract*, not just presentation. A single `style` prop won't cover it; you'll need a discriminated variant on the props type. And **Recently Viewed Full History has no spec to build against at all** — flag it as blocked before it's committed to a sprint.</result>

### §5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts
> All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

> * **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.

> * **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.

> * **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.

### §5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts
> All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

> * **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.

> * **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.

> * **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.

**1. Does browsing history / Recently Viewed require consent before it can be stored?**
**Undecided, and formally so.** Open item #1 on 04.6 is exactly this question, owned by Zimmermann Legal, unresolved. The current Magento behaviour is *no gating* (Jasmijn Tsang tested AU and EU domestic on 3 Jul 2026 and confirmed history was still tracked after rejecting all cookies). Every rule that exists is scoped to **third-party scripts** — TSD §11.1: *"No third-party tracking or marketing script loads until consent is granted"*; 04.1.17: *"Third-party tracking and marketing scripts will only load after customer consent is granted."* A first-party session store or SFCC customer attribute is not a third-party script, so **nothing in the documentation either permits or forbids it.** No document anywhere mentions `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` or client-side storage.

**5. Regional differences?**
**REG-054** is the one place defaults are specified:

**REG-066** requires a consent audit log: *"recording when and how consent was captured."* If Recently Viewed ends up gated, its consent state has to be auditable.

**REG-051** also confirms the taxonomy problem is structural: the only configurable categories are *"Performance Cookies, Analytics Cookies, and Marketing Cookies. Required Cookies are non-configurable."* There is no functional/personalisation bucket for a first-party history store to sit in.

## One thing to disregard from the CRM reader

That agent flagged a "conflict" — that the marketing opt-in rows on 04.1.11 specify no default state, contradicting AGENTS.md's US-pre-checked rule. **That is not a conflict.** The rule lives on 04.1.6 as **REG-057**: *"The checkbox will be unchecked by default for all storefronts except US, where it will be pre-checked."* The CRM page simply isn't where that rule is documented. AGENTS.md is correct.

## What 04.1.11 (CRM, v16) added

My keyword scan and the full read agree: **zero** occurrences of consent, cookie, Didomi, GDPR, erasure, DSAR, retention, browsing, or recently. It offers no cover at all. Two useful things did come out of it:

**The only retention figure that exists anywhere in the documentation** is CRM-140's Comments column, and it is for wishlist, not browsing history, and it is a suggestion rather than a requirement:
> Suggested threshold 18 months - OOTB SFCC for guest users is 7 days for logged in users we need to define custom logic to clear wishlist

The requirement text itself (*"a configurable rule for automatic removal of wishlist items after a defined period of inactivity"*) names no period.

**Wishlist is the structural precedent for exactly what you're proposing.** CRM-139 persists it globally for registered customers across sessions, devices and regions; CRM-119/CRM-129 prompt guests to log in instead. Same guest/authenticated split. And the authenticated-side purge is explicitly unsolved there too — so Recently Viewed would inherit an already-open question rather than hit a new one.

Also confirmed: Omneo is system of record for the customer profile with SFCC holding a synced local copy, but **wishlist data is SFCC-only** (CRM-025) — which is the closest analogue for where account-persisted browsing history would live.

# Confluence coverage for SFCC-236 / SFCC-83 / SFCC-84

**Caveat on dates:** the Confluence API returned empty `created`/`updated` fields for every page in this space. I report **version numbers** and **dates stated in the page body** instead. Where I say "no last-updated date", that means none is recoverable.

## 1. TSDs — the headline is an absence

**There is no TSD for product card, product tile, shared components, recently viewed, or browsing history. None. Not under the TSD parent, not anywhere in the space.**

The TSD parent **392888324** has 15 children; I enumerated all of them. Three further TSDs sit outside that parent (`TSD-SFCC-708` 458948614, `SFCC-49 Country List` 453443668, `TSD: AI-Assisted Defect Triage` 277708843). The full TSD set is enumerable and none covers your three stories.

Nearest neighbours, both PDP-scoped feature TSDs, neither addressing a card container or a variant API:

| Page | ID | Ver | Body date | Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TSD-SFCC-225 — Product Badges** | 446791683 | 5 | Created 26 Aug 2026, **v0.4 Draft, sign-off Pending** | Scopes badges to **PDP only**. Delivers `c_productBadges` via the `dw.ocapi.shop.product.modifyGETResponse` hook and renders pills above the product name. |
| TSD-SFCC-708 — PDP Related Colours | 458948614 | — | Created 31 Aug 2026, v0.3 Draft | Cross-linked swatch navigation, PDP only |
| **Technical Solution Design – PWA** | 256835585 | 11 | "Last updated 2026-07-16" | Architecture only. I grepped it: **zero occurrences** of recently viewed, browsing history, product tile, or product card. One wishlist mention, and it is a rendering-pattern rule (below). |

**A concrete technical trap in the badge TSD.** SPR-16 requires badges **on tiles**. TSD-SFCC-225 delivers badges only on the product **GET** response. PLP/search grids are populated from product *search*, not product GET — so `c_productBadges` will not be present in tile data. If the shared card renders badges, that is unsolved server-side work that no story currently owns.

**One TSD line that does bear on SFCC-84.** TSD 256835585 assigns rendering patterns by page type: PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages get **Full SSR**; "Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book" get **SSR shell + CSR data**. A personalised browsing-history page falls in the second group, while the recently-viewed rail in SFCC-83 has to mount on Full-SSR pages — a personalisation-on-SSR tension nothing has designed for.

## 3. Recently Viewed — storage, retention, consent

### Where it is stored: not designed anywhere

The **only** storage statement in the entire space is the SPR-61 clause: *"stored in the browser session and persisted cross-session on login."* That is it.

- **No SFCC customer profile custom attribute** is named anywhere.
- **No Einstein, Omneo, or Data Cloud** involvement is documented for browsing history. (Einstein appears only for recommendations and search — SPR-42, SPR-58, SPR-63.)
- `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / "session storage" appear **nowhere** in any requirement page or in the PWA TSD.
- No cap, no dedupe rule, no cross-region behaviour, and **no anonymous→authenticated merge rule** — despite that merge being the single hardest part of the feature.

### Retention: no period is documented anywhere

Exhaustively checked. The only retention requirement is **REG-062**: *"The system will allow data retention periods to be configured in SFCC Business Manager per market. Customer PII will be automatically purged upon expiry of the configured retention period."* — it defers the value entirely and nobody has supplied one.

For contrast, wishlist *does* have a number: **CRM-140** comment — *"Suggested threshold 18 months - OOTB SFCC for guest users is 7 days for logged in users we need to define custom logic to clear wishlist."* Recently Viewed has no equivalent.

**Unflagged consequence:** if history is written against the customer account, it becomes PII and inherits **REG-060** (right-to-erasure), **REG-065** (DSAR export) and **REG-062** (per-market purge). No document acknowledges this, and TSD §11.3 pushes GDPR fulfilment out of PWA scope entirely.

### Consent: a formally open question owned by Legal

`04.6 Consent Management — Business Overview`, ID **299433985**, v6 (no last-updated date, zero comments, zero children). In its assessment table:

| Feature | Category | On site? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Recently Viewed products** | **`Required?`** | ✅ | ⚠️ "Currently tracks even when consent is dismissed or rejected on AU/EU — confirm intended behaviour" |

The category cell literally reads `Required?` — a guess, not an assignment. And **Open item #1**, owner **Zimmermann Legal**:

> "Confirm intended behaviour for **Recently Viewed** when consent is not granted — should tracking be suppressed? Current Magento AU site tracks regardless of consent."

**Unresolved in every version to v6.** For contrast the same table classes Wishlist as "Required — functional, no consent needed" and Einstein "You May Also Like" as "Analytics — consent needed". Recently Viewed sits between them, undecided.

**The resolution is tracked in Jira, not Confluence, and it is blocked.** SFCC-83 originally carried consent ACs; they were moved out on 14 Jul into **SFCC-106 "Consent Gating for PWA-Loaded Tracking & Personalisation Components"**, whose status is **Blocked** pending a Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley consent review. Its draft AC has guests-without-consent seeing **no Recently Viewed rail at all**, no authenticated-shopper AC, and no retention value. The 13 Jul consent meeting (page 346587138) records the item as *"postponed - consent review is in progress with TNL / Zimmermann."*

## 6. Consent gating that would apply

`04.1.6 Regional Storefronts`, ID **303104002**, v14 owns the consent requirements (prefix **REG**, not `CNS` — that prefix does not exist).

- **REG-049**: *"The system will only load **third-party** tracking and marketing scripts after the customer has granted consent via Didomi."* — scoped to third-party scripts. A first-party session store is neither permitted nor forbidden.
- **REG-051**: categories are **Performance, Analytics, Marketing**; Required is non-configurable. **There is no Functional or Personalisation category** to file browsing history under.
- **REG-054**: EU opted-**out** by default; AU, US International, HK, ME opted-**in** by default; US domestic requires explicit choice, no action = opted-out. **UK is not named** — a real gap for a separate storefront under UK GDPR/PECR.
- TSD §11.1 sets the safety default: *"Where consent state cannot be determined, the system **fails closed**."* §11.4: Didomi purpose IDs are *"**TBC — none have been received from Zimmermann yet.**"*
- **AAB-003** (04.1.10, ID 302710790): the data layer is populated *regardless* of consent; Didomi gates at the tag layer. # Contradictions with the ticket summaries

These are the ones that should change the plan.

### SFCC-236 — the "one shared component with four variants" framing exists in no document

Four different names are in play, in four different places, with four different variant axes:

- `04.7 Component Inventory` (ID **400195591**, v13, in-body 2026-08-10) models it as **three separate modules** — **Product Card Base** (Variants cell literally `—`), **Product Card Group** (variants: *"3-up, 4-up"*, a grid density), **Product Cards with Lookbook**. All three are listed as **PDP only**.
- `04.2 Design Tracker` (ID **258801666**, v44) calls it **Product Tile**, owns it under the **PLP** epic, and lists variants as *"per-colour variant tiles; hover image vs video; large/featured merchandised tile variant"*.
- `04.2` also lists **"wishlist item card with availability"** as a **separate component** under the Wishlist epic (SFCC-8).
- `04.72` states the one-component principle but names **PDP, PLP and Homepage** — three surfaces. **Wishlist and Recently Viewed Full History are not in that list.**

**Wishlist is the outlier that breaks a single style prop.** It needs printed size + colour (CRM-132) which PLP encodes by tile identity instead (SPR-11), a "What's Now price" type that appears in no PRC row, a region-unavailable greyed state (CRM-134), a VIC price state (PRC-17), and a destructive add-to-bag (CRM-137). Three of those change the **data contract**, not the presentation. This wants a discriminated union on the props type, not a `style` string.

### SFCC-236 — a blocking, unresolved conflict on the PLP tile's icon

**SPR-14 / SPR-15** were updated to say the PLP tile carries a **cart** icon, with wishlist explicitly struck: *"wishlist on product card in PLP is not part of the new designs."*
**CRM-113 / 114 / 115 / 117 / 118** are all still live, unstruck and Confirmed, and still say the **wishlist star** sits on the PLP tile with an in-stock-sizes popover.

Both pages are "source of truth", both extracted 3 Jul 2026. This decides whether the card's action slot is one icon or two. Route to Dani Rivett / Jasmijn Tsang before estimating.

### SFCC-236 — three of the four variants are behind future design-lock dates

04.72's tracker: PDP finalised Aug 13 (passed); **PLP Sep 7**, **Homepage Sep 7**, **Wishlist Sep 21**. Today is 2 Sep. 04.72's own hard rule says stories are written against locked designs only. `1.5 Web Design (UX)` (ID **268075023**, v2) has **Wishlist at DRAFT / "Not ready for build"**.

### SFCC-236 — Homepage may not be a commerce component at all

`5.9.3` (2026-09-02, the newest relevant doc) flags a **"Shoppable product caption / product-grid carousel"** as *"the single most consistent pattern with zero Jira coverage — 97 of 299 pages"* — and places it in the Contentful folder, which by that page's own statement **cannot reuse the SFCC-side components**. Meanwhile **HPC-001** carries an open comment: *"Open Discussion: Product Names/Prices - SFCC vs Contentful."* Whether a homepage product card even sources its data from SFCC is unresolved.

### SFCC-83 — the surface list is wrong three ways

| Source | Surfaces |
|---|---|
| **Ticket** | PLP, PDP, Cart |
| **SPR-61 (the signed-off FR)** | **PDP and Cart only** |
| 04.7 Component Inventory | **PDP only** |
| 04.2 Design Tracker, Recommendation Carousels row | **PDP, cart, mini-bag, and account** |

**PLP appears on no documented list.** Mini-bag and account appear on the docs' list but not the ticket's.

### SFCC-83 — "cross-device, stored against the customer account" is not backed

SPR-61 says *"persisted cross-session on login."* It does **not** say cross-device, and does **not** say stored against the customer account. Both are additions the ticket makes. (Contrast **CRM-139**, which for wishlist explicitly says *"across sessions, devices, store view switches and regions"* — the vocabulary exists in this project when it is meant.)

### SFCC-83 — PRD-027 and SPR-61 disagree with each other

PRD-027 says session history only. SPR-61 says session **plus** cross-session persistence on login. Both Confirmed, neither struck through.

### SFCC-83 — it is downstream of a Blocked story

SFCC-106 holds the consent ACs that were deliberately removed from SFCC-83 on 14 Jul, and it is **Blocked** pending the TNL/Zimmermann consent review. Building SFCC-83 without that outcome means guessing whether the rail renders at all for a non-consenting guest.

### SFCC-84 — the page is undocumented scope, and its core design question is open since June

- Not in `04.1.18 Storefront Page Templates`, the confirmed page-template list.
- Not in `04.7 Component Inventory` — no module, no template row.
- Not in `04.72` — no epic covers it.
- The only guidance is two unanswered questions on `04.2`: *"2 options: Wishlist/Search Results … Look like the wishlist or like a search page"*, and *"Conscious choice for minimal info, no price no product name?"*, closing with **"07-07: Full history still pending."**

That second question also feeds back into SFCC-236: if the recently-viewed card genuinely drops price and product name, that is a **content-reduction variant**, not a styling variant.

### Cross-cutting — design status is contradictory, and the newer page is not the authoritative one

`04.7` says Product Card and Recently Viewed are **✅ Done (confirmed by Dennis 2026-08-10)**. `04.2` says **PENDING with Zimmermann sign-off Pending** on every corresponding row. `04.2` is where client sign-off is actually recorded (v44 vs v13). Do not read "Done" on 04.7 as sign-off.

### Cross-cutting — no Confluence page references any of the three stories

A CQL body search for `SFCC-236`, `SFCC-83`, `SFCC-84` returns nothing relevant. These three stories have **zero documentation footprint outside Jira**.

## 2. The requirement IDs — all located and quoted

Three different pages own the prefixes. All three carry the same provenance line: *"extracted from Zimmermann Functional Requirements excel, downloaded July 3rd, 2026 after all requirements were confirmed."* Strikethrough = out of scope.

### SPR — `04.1.9 Search and Recommendations`, ID **303661057**, v14

| ID | Requirement (verbatim) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **SPR-01** | "The system will support dedicated landing page for each category, listing all products in that category in a grid layout" | Confirmed |
| **SPR-02** | "The system will support a 'view more' pattern on the product listing page that loads more products." | Confirmed — comment: *"number of view more is custom build, it's handled in FE. Dani has suggested 36. Needs confirmation"* |
| **SPR-10** | "The system will support showing product image, name, and price for each product tile" | Confirmed |
| **SPR-11** | "The system will show each possible colour variant for a product as a separate tile" | Confirmed |
| **SPR-12** | "The system will surface markdown pricing on product tiles within the Product Listing Page (PLP), displaying both the original retail price ("Was...") and the reduced sale price ("Now...")" | Confirmed |
| **SPR-13** | "The system will, on hover in desktop, alternate between the model and flat/item image variants stored per product tile." | Confirmed |
| **SPR-14** | "The system will display a ~~save-to-wishlist~~ **cart** icon on each product tile on the PLP" | Confirmed — comment: *"Changed FR to cart icon - wishlist on product card in PLP is not part of the new designs"* |
| **SPR-16** | "The system will support ~~clickable~~ product badges (RUNWAY, CAMPAIGN, etc.) on tiles, driven by configurable product attributes in Business Manager; a product can be assigned multipled badges" | Confirmed |
| **SPR-61** | "The system must display "Recently Viewed" products on **the PDP and Cart page**; browsing history to be stored in the browser session and persisted cross-session on login" | Confirmed |

Also load-bearing and not on your label list: **SPR-15** (size prompt on cart-icon tap, SKU-level), **SPR-17** (Quick Add to Bag with size prompt), **SPR-56** (search tile = image, name, price — effectively identical to SPR-10), **SPR-31** (out-of-stock products *demoted or suppressed* in category/search).

### PRD — `04.1.8 Product, Catalogue and PDP`, ID **302776322**, v18

**PRD-027**, Sub-area *Content Modules*, Accenture, ALL, Custom, **Confirmed**, not struck through:

> "The system should display a "Recently Viewed" carousel based on the customer's browsing session history."
> **Comments: "Updated design: not a carousel but with button "See full history""**

That comment is the **sole documentary basis for SFCC-84's entire existence**. The requirement text itself was never rewritten and still says "carousel" while sitting at Confirmed. PRD-027 is the only row on the page mentioning recently viewed, browsing history, or session history. The page holds 71 rows (PRD-001→071, no gaps) and contains **no product tile or product card requirement at all**.

### PRC — `04.1.12 Price, Currency and Promotions`, ID **302612483**, v11

**PRC-09**, Confirmed, Custom:
> "The system will display the original list price alongside the active sale price when a sale pricebook entry is active; this will appear on product tiles (PLP), PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended product tiles and order history."
> Comment: *"Sale items usually excluded from recommendations (manual rule)"*

Two more that constrain the card's price slot: **PRC-08** and **PRC-33** (same surface list, consistent display), and critically **PRC-17** — customer-group/VIC pricing must show "consistently across PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended product tiles and wishlist", with **PRC-18** adding "Customer group discounts will prevail over sale pricing." So the price slot needs **three states plus a precedence rule**, not two.

**Homepage appears in none of the PRC surface lists.**

---

## 3. Recently Viewed — storage, retention, consent

### Where it is stored: not designed anywhere

The **only** storage statement in the entire space is the SPR-61 clause: *"stored in the browser session and persisted cross-session on login."* That is it.

- **No SFCC customer profile custom attribute** is named anywhere.
- **No Einstein, Omneo, or Data Cloud** involvement is documented for browsing history. (Einstein appears only for recommendations and search — SPR-42, SPR-58, SPR-63.)
- `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / "session storage" appear **nowhere** in any requirement page or in the PWA TSD.
- No cap, no dedupe rule, no cross-region behaviour, and **no anonymous→authenticated merge rule** — despite that merge being the single hardest part of the feature.

### Retention: no period is documented anywhere

Exhaustively checked. The only retention requirement is **REG-062**: *"The system will allow data retention periods to be configured in SFCC Business Manager per market. Customer PII will be automatically purged upon expiry of the configured retention period."* — it defers the value entirely and nobody has supplied one.

For contrast, wishlist *does* have a number: **CRM-140** comment — *"Suggested threshold 18 months - OOTB SFCC for guest users is 7 days for logged in users we need to define custom logic to clear wishlist."* Recently Viewed has no equivalent.

**Unflagged consequence:** if history is written against the customer account, it becomes PII and inherits **REG-060** (right-to-erasure), **REG-065** (DSAR export) and **REG-062** (per-market purge). No document acknowledges this, and TSD §11.3 pushes GDPR fulfilment out of PWA scope entirely.

### Consent: a formally open question owned by Legal

`04.6 Consent Management — Business Overview`, ID **299433985**, v6 (no last-updated date, zero comments, zero children). In its assessment table:

| Feature | Category | On site? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Recently Viewed products** | **`Required?`** | ✅ | ⚠️ "Currently tracks even when consent is dismissed or rejected on AU/EU — confirm intended behaviour" |

The category cell literally reads `Required?` — a guess, not an assignment. And **Open item #1**, owner **Zimmermann Legal**:

> "Confirm intended behaviour for **Recently Viewed** when consent is not granted — should tracking be suppressed? Current Magento AU site tracks regardless of consent."

**Unresolved in every version to v6.** For contrast the same table classes Wishlist as "Required — functional, no consent needed" and Einstein "You May Also Like" as "Analytics — consent needed". Recently Viewed sits between them, undecided.

**The resolution is tracked in Jira, not Confluence, and it is blocked.** SFCC-83 originally carried consent ACs; they were moved out on 14 Jul into **SFCC-106 "Consent Gating for PWA-Loaded Tracking & Personalisation Components"**, whose status is **Blocked** pending a Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley consent review. Its draft AC has guests-without-consent seeing **no Recently Viewed rail at all**, no authenticated-shopper AC, and no retention value. The 13 Jul consent meeting (page 346587138) records the item as *"postponed - consent review is in progress with TNL / Zimmermann."*

---

## 4. Component reuse / design system — no such page exists

**There is no design-system page, no atomic-structure page, and no component-build standard.** Zero pages titled "design system", "atomic", "atoms/molecules/organisms", "storybook", "style guide", "ui kit", or "pattern library". Verified against the complete 284-page space tree plus body-text search.

What exists instead, and all of it is partial or stale:

| Page | ID | Ver | What it gives you — and what is wrong with it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Development Standards** | 261750785 | 2 | Naming, TS-only, Storybook categories, tiers. **Stale twice over:** tells you to import icons from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` (AGENTS.md now forbids this), and its worked token example uses bare Chakra keys (`color="brand.primary"`), which `overrideStyling.md` now forbids and `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build on. |
| **Component Override Strategy** | 261881857 | 4 | The only page describing how to physically build a component — copy-first override procedure, keep kebab-case. **Stale on the point that matters:** says new components go in `overrides/app/components/custom/`. The repo uses `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/`. |
| **04.71 Writing User Stories for Components** | 400195600 | 2 | Level 1 component epics vs Level 2 page epics. A PWA-Kit-only component gets **one story in the PWA Kit epic**. Directly supports SFCC-236's shape. |
| **04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker** | 408944644 | 6 | Holds the actual reuse governance — quoted below. |
| **5.9.3 — Component Mapping** | 464945168 | 7 | Body-dated **2026-09-02**. The only page in the space using atoms/molecules/organisms vocabulary — and it scopes that to Contentful, not commerce. |
| **Design Decision Tracker** | 449282049 | 1 | **Completely empty.** Third child of 04.7, created and never filled. |

**The reuse rules that do exist**, from 04.72, verbatim:

> "Each component is owned by the **earliest epic in the sequence where it appears**. That epic is responsible for designing all variations of that component — including any variations needed by later epics. For example, if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage, all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP."

> "**Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only. Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component."

**And the position 5.9.3 records, which cuts the other way:** the SFCC-side components under `overrides/app/components/` "weren't built to stand alone, and we can't reuse them for pure-Contentful pages" — Contentful gets a parallel set under `overrides/app/components/contentful/components/`. Its heading is **"Sharing tokens, not components."**

---

## 5. Tile contents per surface

| Surface | Spec exists? | Source | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PLP** | Yes | SPR-10/11/12/13/14/16/17 | image, name, price, was/now, per-colour-variant tiles, hover model↔flat swap, badges, cart icon + size popover, quick add |
| **Search** | Yes | SPR-56, SPR-55 | image, name, price — effectively identical to PLP |
| **Wishlist** | Yes, as a requirement row | **CRM-132** (04.1.11, ID **302022672**, v16) | "product image, product name, price, sale price or **What's Now price** where applicable, **size** and **colour** for each item" |
| **Homepage** | **NO** | — | `04.1.1 Homepage and Content` (ID **303071234**, v14) has 40 rows, HPC-001→040, and **not one product tile requirement**. Closest is HPC-009: *"editorial modules including campaign imagery, collection features and product spotlights"* — no contents, no selection logic. |
| **Recently Viewed rail** | **NO** | — | SPR-61 says only *that* it displays, never what a tile contains |
| **See Full History page** | **NO** | — | Nothing beyond PRD-027's comment |

Wishlist also carries states no other tile has: **CRM-131 / CRM-134** require a **greyed-out "unavailable in your region"** item that stays visible — the exact inverse of SPR-31, which suppresses out-of-stock products from PLP. And **CRM-136/137**: add-to-bag from wishlist **removes the item**, a destructive side effect a PLP quick-add must not have.

**Wishlist page layout is undocumented.** No CRM row says grid, tile, card, or columns. `04.1.18 Storefront Page Templates` (ID **303333385**, v3) confirms a wishlist template will be delivered but not its shape — and its My Account list is *"login, registration, password reset, order history, order details, returns history, address book, saved payments and wishlist."* **No browsing-history page.**

---

## 6. Consent gating that would apply

`04.1.6 Regional Storefronts`, ID **303104002**, v14 owns the consent requirements (prefix **REG**, not `CNS` — that prefix does not exist).

- **REG-049**: *"The system will only load **third-party** tracking and marketing scripts after the customer has granted consent via Didomi."* — scoped to third-party scripts. A first-party session store is neither permitted nor forbidden.
- **REG-051**: categories are **Performance, Analytics, Marketing**; Required is non-configurable. **There is no Functional or Personalisation category** to file browsing history under.
- **REG-054**: EU opted-**out** by default; AU, US International, HK, ME opted-**in** by default; US domestic requires explicit choice, no action = opted-out. **UK is not named** — a real gap for a separate storefront under UK GDPR/PECR.
- TSD §11.1 sets the safety default: *"Where consent state cannot be determined, the system **fails closed**."* §11.4: Didomi purpose IDs are *"**TBC — none have been received from Zimmermann yet.**"*
- **AAB-003** (04.1.10, ID 302710790): the data layer is populated *regardless* of consent; Didomi gates at the tag layer. Note the GA4 event pages (`view_item_list` 454918148, `select_item` 453804038, `add_to_cart` 454098963) all require `item_list_name` to read "Recently Viewed" — so the rail must emit analytics even where the rail itself may be gated.

---

# Contradictions with the ticket summaries

These are the ones that should change the plan.

### SFCC-236 — the "one shared component with four variants" framing exists in no document

Four different names are in play, in four different places, with four different variant axes:

- `04.7 Component Inventory` (ID **400195591**, v13, in-body 2026-08-10) models it as **three separate modules** — **Product Card Base** (Variants cell literally `—`), **Product Card Group** (variants: *"3-up, 4-up"*, a grid density), **Product Cards with Lookbook**. All three are listed as **PDP only**.
- `04.2 Design Tracker` (ID **258801666**, v44) calls it **Product Tile**, owns it under the **PLP** epic, and lists variants as *"per-colour variant tiles; hover image vs video; large/featured merchandised tile variant"*.
- `04.2` also lists **"wishlist item card with availability"** as a **separate component** under the Wishlist epic (SFCC-8).
- `04.72` states the one-component principle but names **PDP, PLP and Homepage** — three surfaces. **Wishlist and Recently Viewed Full History are not in that list.**

**Wishlist is the outlier that breaks a single style prop.** It needs printed size + colour (CRM-132) which PLP encodes by tile identity instead (SPR-11), a "What's Now price" type that appears in no PRC row, a region-unavailable greyed state (CRM-134), a VIC price state (PRC-17), and a destructive add-to-bag (CRM-137). Three of those change the **data contract**, not the presentation. This wants a discriminated union on the props type, not a `style` string.

### SFCC-236 — a blocking, unresolved conflict on the PLP tile's icon

**SPR-14 / SPR-15** were updated to say the PLP tile carries a **cart** icon, with wishlist explicitly struck: *"wishlist on product card in PLP is not part of the new designs."*
**CRM-113 / 114 / 115 / 117 / 118** are all still live, unstruck and Confirmed, and still say the **wishlist star** sits on the PLP tile with an in-stock-sizes popover.

Both pages are "source of truth", both extracted 3 Jul 2026. This decides whether the card's action slot is one icon or two. Route to Dani Rivett / Jasmijn Tsang before estimating.

### SFCC-236 — three of the four variants are behind future design-lock dates

04.72's tracker: PDP finalised Aug 13 (passed); **PLP Sep 7**, **Homepage Sep 7**, **Wishlist Sep 21**. Today is 2 Sep. 04.72's own hard rule says stories are written against locked designs only. `1.5 Web Design (UX)` (ID **268075023**, v2) has **Wishlist at DRAFT / "Not ready for build"**.

### SFCC-236 — Homepage may not be a commerce component at all

`5.9.3` (2026-09-02, the newest relevant doc) flags a **"Shoppable product caption / product-grid carousel"** as *"the single most consistent pattern with zero Jira coverage — 97 of 299 pages"* — and places it in the Contentful folder, which by that page's own statement **cannot reuse the SFCC-side components**. Meanwhile **HPC-001** carries an open comment: *"Open Discussion: Product Names/Prices - SFCC vs Contentful."* Whether a homepage product card even sources its data from SFCC is unresolved.

### SFCC-83 — the surface list is wrong three ways

| Source | Surfaces |
|---|---|
| **Ticket** | PLP, PDP, Cart |
| **SPR-61 (the signed-off FR)** | **PDP and Cart only** |
| 04.7 Component Inventory | **PDP only** |
| 04.2 Design Tracker, Recommendation Carousels row | **PDP, cart, mini-bag, and account** |

**PLP appears on no documented list.** Mini-bag and account appear on the docs' list but not the ticket's.

### SFCC-83 — "cross-device, stored against the customer account" is not backed

SPR-61 says *"persisted cross-session on login."* It does **not** say cross-device, and does **not** say stored against the customer account. Both are additions the ticket makes. (Contrast **CRM-139**, which for wishlist explicitly says *"across sessions, devices, store view switches and regions"* — the vocabulary exists in this project when it is meant.)

### SFCC-83 — PRD-027 and SPR-61 disagree with each other

PRD-027 says session history only. SPR-61 says session **plus** cross-session persistence on login. Both Confirmed, neither struck through.

### SFCC-83 — it is downstream of a Blocked story

SFCC-106 holds the consent ACs that were deliberately removed from SFCC-83 on 14 Jul, and it is **Blocked** pending the TNL/Zimmermann consent review. Building SFCC-83 without that outcome means guessing whether the rail renders at all for a non-consenting guest.

### SFCC-84 — the page is undocumented scope, and its core design question is open since June

- Not in `04.1.18 Storefront Page Templates`, the confirmed page-template list.
- Not in `04.7 Component Inventory` — no module, no template row.
- Not in `04.72` — no epic covers it.
- The only guidance is two unanswered questions on `04.2`: *"2 options: Wishlist/Search Results … Look like the wishlist or like a search page"*, and *"Conscious choice for minimal info, no price no product name?"*, closing with **"07-07: Full history still pending."**

That second question also feeds back into SFCC-236: if the recently-viewed card genuinely drops price and product name, that is a **content-reduction variant**, not a styling variant.

### Cross-cutting — design status is contradictory, and the newer page is not the authoritative one

`04.7` says Product Card and Recently Viewed are **✅ Done (confirmed by Dennis 2026-08-10)**. `04.2` says **PENDING with Zimmermann sign-off Pending** on every corresponding row. `04.2` is where client sign-off is actually recorded (v44 vs v13). Do not read "Done" on 04.7 as sign-off.

### Cross-cutting — no Confluence page references any of the three stories

A CQL body search for `SFCC-236`, `SFCC-83`, `SFCC-84` returns nothing relevant. These three stories have **zero documentation footprint outside Jira**.

---

## Explicit "nothing exists" list

1. **No TSD for product card / product tile / shared components.**
2. **No TSD or design doc for recently viewed or browsing-history storage.**
3. **No design-system, atomic-structure, or component-build-standards page** — only two stale pages (261750785, 261881857) that contradict the repo on folder structure, icon imports and tokens. The repo's `.claude/rules/` is the real standard and Confluence never caught up.
4. **No Homepage product tile spec.**
5. **No Wishlist page layout spec** (contents exist via CRM-132; layout does not).
6. **No "See Full History" page spec** — no requirement, no template row, no design, no route, no pagination.
7. **No retention period for browsing history, or any personal data.**
8. **No consent treatment for first-party storage** — every rule addresses third-party scripts. Structural gap, not a one-page oversight.
9. **No UK Didomi consent default** in REG-054.
10. **`Design Decision Tracker` (449282049) is an empty page** — created for exactly these decisions, never filled.</result>

I'm not handing this to `zimmerMANNBuild`, and I haven't written a plan. Planning against this would be planning the wrong thing.

## The two that should sting

**Your own governance rule forbids starting.** Confluence 04.72 says plainly: *"User stories are written against locked designs only."* Wishlist doesn't lock until **21 Sep** — two weeks after Sprint 4 ends. PLP and Homepage lock **7 Sep**, the sprint's last day. So SFCC-236's 8 points are committed against three designs that aren't lockable inside the sprint.

**On the icon conflict** — this isn't a doc being vague, it's two "confirmed" sources actively disagreeing. SPR-14 was *amended* to a cart icon, wishlist struck through, with the note *"wishlist on product card in PLP is not part of the new designs."* Meanwhile CRM-113/114/115/117/118 are all still live, unstruck, Confirmed, still specifying a wishlist star with an in-stock-size popover. Both extracted the same day. That decides whether the card's action slot holds one icon or two — you can't build the card without knowing.

## Two traps worth knowing regardless of what you decide

**`CardBaseline` doesn't exist.** Neither does `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`. `CardBaseline` appears three times in the whole repo — all prose in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (128, 181, 186), describing a file nobody wrote. **Building at the SFCC path detonates six pages silently.** The instant `overrides/app/components/product-tile/index.tsx` exists, the resolver redirects PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results to it. And `pages/product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports `{Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}` — **an override without that named export breaks PLP at import time.** Building in `ui-kits/` avoids all of it.

`zimmProductName`, `zimmProductPrice`, `zimmProductDescription`, `zimmColourSwatch`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup`, `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon` all exist and are registered. Parked. Everything's captured in `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/findings.md` — full 29-row gate, the Figma node table to paste against, tier/ownership map, and the reuse list. Nothing needs re-deriving when you're back.

One thing to set expectations: **the links only clear blocker #1.** The other six need decisions or other people, and none of them depend on the Figma URLs — so they're all parallelisable while you're chasing links:

- **Dani / Jasmijn** — cart icon vs wishlist star. This one's the cheapest to close and it gates the card's action slot entirely.
- **Jasmijn** — SFCC-83's surface list, and whether SFCC-84 gets a spec at all.
- **Integration / architecture** — where browsing history actually lives. There's no API, no hook, no TSD, and no owner; this is very likely a backend story that doesn't exist yet.
- **Legal / TNL** — SFCC-106. Not something we can route around.

And separately from this build: the Design System really does have three components called `WishlistOLD` and six overlapping product-card sets. That's what turned "get the Figma node" from a lookup into a blocker, and it's worth Kiera hearing regardless of what we decide here.

Two smaller things I noticed and left alone, since they're outside this build:

- `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` lines 128/181/186 assert a `product-tile` override and a `CardBaseline` export that have never existed. It's Tier 1 Governance, so it needs its own change — but it will mislead the next person who reads it.
- You're still on the merged `SFCC-91` branch. I didn't cut a new one; the skill's rule is not to create branches unasked.

Ping me with the links when you have them and I'll pick up from the gate.

      "value": "What we need to finalise user stories per epic
----------------------------------------------

PWA Kit user stories cannot be written, reviewed or signed off until the relevant design components are locked. Here is what that means in practice.

### 1 — Components must be finalised first

* Before user stories can be written for an epic e.g. Checkout Flow & Delivery, **every UI component that appears in that epic must be finalised in the UI kit** — fully componentised in Figma with all variations, states and responsive sizes accounted for. This allows us to build the component user story.
* Each component is owned by the **earliest epic in the sequence where it appears**. That epic is responsible for designing all variations of that component — including any variations needed by later epics. For example, if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage, all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP.

> As we move through the epic sequence, design effort should reduce. By the time we reach epics like Homepage or Wishlist, most components should already exist. Design at that stage should be limited to anything genuinely net-new.

### 2 — Design freeze

* **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only. Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component.

### 3 — Sign-off checklist per epic

* Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.
